summary: Lithuania is an EU and Schengen member: EU/EFTA citizens enter freely, around 60 visa-exempt nationalities can stay 90 days in any 180-day period, and everyone else needs a €90 Schengen visa. Entry from Belarus and Russia is restricted, and most Russian citizens are barred from entering even with a valid Schengen visa.

defaultStayWindow.text: 90 days in any rolling 180-day period, counted across the whole Schengen Area rather than per country. The day you arrive counts as the first day and the day you leave counts as the last. Leaving and coming back does not reset the allowance: on any given day, days already spent anywhere in the area during the preceding 180 still count against the 90.

source.name: European Commission — Schengen short-stay calculator (DG Migration and Home Affairs)

fee.notes: Children 6–11: €45; under 6: free. Fee set EU-wide since June 11, 2024.
For stays over 90 days: work, study and other long-stay purposes. Confirm the current fee and category with the Lithuanian mission before applying.

source.name: Migration Department under the Ministry of the Interior of Lithuania

passportValidity.text: Non-EU passports must be valid for at least 3 months beyond your planned departure from the Schengen Area and have been issued within the last 10 years.

source.name: Migration Department under the Ministry of the Interior of Lithuania

travelInsurance.text: Schengen visa applicants must hold travel medical insurance covering at least €30,000, valid across the Schengen Area for the whole stay. Visa-exempt visitors are not required to show it but border officers may ask about cover.

onwardTicket.text: Border officers may ask non-EU visitors for proof of return or onward travel and accommodation details.

source.name: Migration Department under the Ministry of the Interior of Lithuania

proofOfFunds.text: Lithuania expects non-EU visitors to show roughly €40 per person per day for the stay; border officers assess sufficiency case by case alongside accommodation and travel bookings. Confirm the current guideline with the Lithuanian mission.

source.name: Migration Department under the Ministry of the Interior of Lithuania

declarations.name: EES — Entry/Exit System (biometric registration)
declarations.submitWindow: At the border on first entry
declarations.text: Non-EU travelers are registered biometrically (fingerprints and photo) in the EU Entry/Exit System at Schengen external borders. Registration happens at the border. There is nothing to submit in advance, but allow extra time on your first entry.

declarations.name: ETIAS — European Travel Information and Authorization System

fee.notes: Free for under-18s and over-70s. Valid 3 years or until passport expiry.

declarations.text: Visa-exempt travelers will need an ETIAS travel authorization to enter the Schengen Area. It is being phased in. Check the official EU site for the current status and apply only there.

currencyLimits.text: Cash of €10,000 or more (or equivalent) must be declared when entering or leaving the EU.

notes: Duty-free from outside the EU: 200 cigarettes, 1 liter of spirits, goods up to €300 (€430 arriving by air/sea).
No limits on goods for personal use when arriving from another EU country.

payments.text: Lithuania is highly cashless. Cards and contactless work everywhere from supermarkets to market stalls; cash is rarely needed outside the smallest rural shops.

safety.text: Lithuania is a very safe destination with low crime; the usual pickpocketing precautions apply in Vilnius' old town and at bus stations. The border zones with Belarus and Russia's Kaliningrad region are the only areas to avoid.

source.name: U.S. Department of State — Lithuania Travel Advisory

bestTimeToVisit.text: May to September is warm and green — midsummer celebrations in June, the Baltic beaches of the Curonian Spit in July–August, and mild city weather for Vilnius and Kaunas into September. Winters are cold and dark.

idp.text: Lithuania is a party to both the 1949 Geneva and the 1968 Vienna Conventions on Road Traffic, so it recognizes an International Driving Permit issued under either.

source.name: UN Treaty Collection — Convention on Road Traffic (Vienna, 1968), status of parties
source.instrument: Convention on Road Traffic, Geneva, 19 September 1949 (UNTS vol. 125, p. 3); Convention on Road Traffic, Vienna, 8 November 1968 (UNTS vol. 1042, p. 17)

driving.text: Lithuania is a party to both the 1949 Geneva and the 1968 Vienna Conventions on Road Traffic, so it recognizes an International Driving Permit issued under either. Whether a permit is required in addition to a national license, and for how long a foreign license may be used, are set by national road law and have not been checked for Lithuania yet.

tips.text: Avoid the borders with Belarus and Russia's Kaliningrad region — several crossings are closed, rules change at short notice, and most Western governments advise against travel to Belarus and Russia altogether.
The Curonian Spit national park charges a vehicle entry fee and shares its peninsula with Russia's Kaliningrad region — do not stray past the marked border at the southern end.
You can go days without cash. Cards and contactless are accepted almost everywhere, including markets and intercity buses.
Apply for ETIAS only at the official travel-europe.europa.eu site once it becomes mandatory — unofficial sites charge inflated fees.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Lithuania?
faq.answer: EU and EFTA citizens enter freely. US, UK, Canadian, Japanese and around 60 other visa-exempt nationalities can stay up to 90 days in any 180-day period across the Schengen Area (with ETIAS being phased in). Everyone else needs a Schengen short-stay visa from the Lithuanian mission serving their place of residence.

faq.question: Can Russian citizens enter Lithuania?
faq.answer: Generally not for tourism. Like the other Baltic states, Lithuania bars most Russian citizens from entering even with a valid Schengen visa — only narrow exceptions apply, such as residence-permit holders, family cases and humanitarian grounds. Check the Migration Department's current rules before planning any travel.

faq.question: How much does a Lithuania Schengen visa cost?
faq.answer: The Schengen short-stay visa costs €90 for adults and €45 for children aged 6–11. A national long-stay (Type D) visa costs around €120. Confirm the current fee with the Lithuanian mission.

faq.question: Is ETIAS required to enter Lithuania?
faq.answer: ETIAS is being phased in for visa-exempt travelers across the Schengen Area. During the transition, travelers without ETIAS are still admitted; once fully mandatory, the €20 online authorization will be required before boarding. Check the official EU website for the current status.

faq.question: Can I cross into Lithuania from Belarus?
faq.answer: Only a limited number of crossing points remain open and lines and checks can be long; rules change at short notice. Most Western governments advise against travel to Belarus entirely. Check advisories and the current list of open crossings before attempting an overland trip.
